discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the prediction of the Higgs mechanism, but the particle itself was established by experiment. Peter Jenni founded and led ATLAS through its design and construction. Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee conceived CMS and drove its design, with Virdee leading the development of its crystal electromagnetic calorimeter. Their detector concepts had to meet exceptional demands in tracking, calorimetry, muon detection and triggering at unprecedented luminosity. They made possible the independent 5-sigma observations in 2012 of a new scalar boson near 125 GeV, whose couplings have since been measured to agree with Standard Model expectations. This work confirmed the last missing element of the Standard Model and opened the Higgs sector to direct experimental study, including the self-coupling that describes the shape of the Higgs potential. The discovery shows what conceptual vision and technical leadership can achieve at the largest scale.
